summary: Gerald James Larson worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Union Theological Seminary and Columbia University, later holding posts at UC Santa Barbara from 1972 and Indiana University Bloomington from 1995.
Gerardus van der Leeuw was a religious studies scholar who studied at Leiden University between circa 1908 and 1916. He held a post at the University of Groningen from 1918 to 1950.
Gerd J. R. Mevissen is an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. His career includes posts at the Free University of Berlin, attested in 2017 and as a Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter in 2026.

Gereon Kopf specializes in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Temple University and mentored by Yasuo Yuasa, he researched at J. F. Oberlin and Nanzan Universities and held posts at Luther College and the University of Hong Kong.

Gergely Hidas is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, later serving as a Khyentse Fellow at Eötvös Loránd University and as a researcher at the British Museum.

Gerhard Meiser was a linguist who pursued his studies at Albertus-Magnus-Gymnasium Regensburg, the University of Munich, the University of Belgrade, the University of Sarajevo, the University of Regensburg, and the University of Freiburg.

Gerhard Oberhammer worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Innsbruck under Erich Frauwallner, at the Sorbonne, and under V. Raghavan, later holding posts at Utrecht University and the University of Vienna.

Gerhard Wolf is a historian and archaeologist who completed his education at Heidelberg University. He held academic posts at Humboldt University of Berlin, Trier University, and the Max Planck Society.

Germaine Dieterlen specialized in religious studies. She pursued her education at the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes and the École Pratique des Hautes Études, studying under Marcel Mauss between circa 1931 and 1939.

Germaine Tillion studied under Marcel Mauss and was educated at the École du Louvre and the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales. She later held a post at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences from circa 1958 to 1977.
Gernot Böhme was a philosopher who studied at the University of Hamburg between circa 1960 and 1965. He later held an academic post at the Technical University of Darmstadt from circa 1977 to 2002.
Gernot Rotter studied at the University of Bonn under Annemarie Schimmel and at the University of Tübingen. He later held a post at the University of Hamburg from circa 1984 to 2006.
Gerrit Jan Meulenbeld was an Indologist who studied at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda. He later served as associate professor of Indology at the University of Groningen from 1978 to 1986.

Gert Klingenschmitt specialized in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Karl Hoffmann and habilitated at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, later holding the chair for Indo-European linguistics at the University of Regensburg.
Geshe Bel-den-drak-ba worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He was a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia in 1987 and served as librarian at Tibet House, New Delhi, attested in 1988.

Geshe Gendün Lodrö specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, training at Drepung Gomang Dratsang under Ngawang Lekden. He served on the faculty at Drepung Gomang, taught at the University of Hamburg, and visited the University of Virginia in 1979.

Geshe Jampa Tegchok was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy who studied at Sera Monastery. He served as abbot and resident teacher at Nalanda Monastery and later as resident teacher at Land of Medicine Buddha.
Geshe Karma Sonam is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. His career includes attested affiliations with the Gyume Tantric College in 1987 and Sera Monastery in 1992.

Geshe Kelsang Gyatso studied at Ngamring Chöde, Jampa Ling, Tashilhunpo, and Sera Monastery under Trijang Rinpoche. Working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he taught at Manjushri Kadampa Meditation Centre and founded the New Kadampa Tradition in 1991.

Geshe Lhakdor studied at the Central School for Tibetans, Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, University of Delhi, and Drepung Loseling. In Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he held posts at Tibet House, New Delhi, UBC, and the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives.
